brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent cells (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with a solid bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full). Dressed with spoon and fork props to show utensil use, verified with check_build meshClash clear.

The configurator checks geometry only and has no material/waterproofing verification. The build uses solid non-drained bins (hex-bin-full) which as a shape helps contain water, but 3D-printed parts are not guaranteed watertight and require user choice of material and post-processing which cannot be verified here.

The configurator cannot verify heat resistance, food safety or dishwasher safety. Parts are 3D-printed plastic in a user-chosen material; heat/UV/dishwasher resistance is not modeled and is never met by geometry alone.

finish.summary: Built a compact 2-cell utensil holder with two solid full-depth bins, capped and joint-bolted. Staged with spoon and fork. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims cannot be met by the configurator – geometry helps containment but material-dependent sealing and heat resistance must be validated by the user.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
